messages:
elena: Quick intake for a customer ask: per-tenant QoS routing + adaptive budgeter. Problem: customers want different tradeoffs (ultra-low p95 latency vs minimal cost) without us exposing low-level knobs. Need clear PRD inputs: goals, non-goals, ACs, and a canary plan.
ryan: Can we be explicit about "adaptive budgeter"? Do we mean assigning token budgets per request or per-session QoS buckets?
elena: Good call. We mean per-route runtime budget that influences routing + early-trim policies (not per-request tokens). Think of it as a QoS profile that affects routing and trimming heuristics.
tess: Non-goal request: no billing UI or invoicing changes this phase. Also we shouldn't introduce tenant-wide admin UI yet. Keep this API-first for small partners.
omar: Operational concern: trimming and fallback can change output quality. We need acceptance criteria around hallucination and failure modes. Also KV cache safety on long contexts is a must.
elena: Draft goals: 1) let early customers pick (low-latency | balanced | low-cost) per-route; 2) runtime will route to compatible model variants or apply controlled trimming; 3) expose minimal cost/latency deltas in Console for transparency.
ryan: Suggest adding a "safe-mode" for fallbacks: if quality drop > X measured via eval set, fallback disabled for that tenant. We can measure via sampling.
tess: UX: keep surface as a single API field qos: "latency"|"balanced"|"cost" plus optional "advanced":true for early adopters. CLI example: `redwood routes create --tenant acme --qos latency`.
ops-bot: Note: runtime currently supports per-route timeouts and model variant labels. No automatic trimming or per-tenant eviction caps yet.
elena: Proposed acceptance criteria (please thumbs):
```
- AC-API: routes.create/update accepts `qos_profile` with values [latency, balanced, cost].
- AC-Routing: "latency" profile routes -> variants with highest perf; p95 <= 220ms on 95th percentile traffic in staging under sampled load.
- AC-Fallback: when primary variant unavailable, runtime switches to compatible variant within 100ms and logs the switch with reason.
- AC-Quality: sampled outputs (1% of responses) show no >5% regression in eval score vs baseline for the tenant's important prompt set during canary.
- AC-Safety: per-tenant KV cache entry cap prevents >50% latency regression under 95th percentile burst traffic.
- AC-Observability: console shows per-tenant cost delta and fallback count for 30d window.
```
ryan: Edge cases to call out: tenants mixing short and very long contexts, tenants with bursty traffic spikes, dedicated pool cold starts, and tenants using streaming vs non-streaming endpoints.
omar: Testing plan: QA harness that replays mixed convo patterns (90% short, 10% long) at varying QPS, and a synthetic failure injection to validate fallback latency and rollback triggers.
tess: Rollout plan idea: API-only alpha -> 3 early customers -> 2-week canary -> open early access. Rollback triggers: p95 > 300ms OR sampled quality regression >5% OR error rate >1.5%.
elena: Owners: eng: @ryan, infra: @omar, design/devex: @tess, metrics: @elena. Timeline ask: spike (1 week) to implement qos field + routing spike, runtime changes (2 sprints), observability + console (1 sprint).
ryan: I'll pick up the routing policy shape and spike on fallback latency measurement.
omar: I'll own the KV cap and evictions + QA harness.
tess: I'll produce CLI + minimal console mock for alpha customers.
elena: Final note: Non-goals reiterated: no tenant billing workflow, no tenant admin UI, no global ML retraining for now. If no objections, I'll capture this as RFC draft tonight.
ryan: +1
omar: +1
tess: +1 :rocket:
